Coram: Hon'Ble Mrs. Justice P Sree Sudha
 Oral Judgment

This appeal is filed against the judgment and award dated 26.07.2016 passed by the III Additional Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru, in MVC No.946/2014.
2.

entities.text: III Additional Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The injured claimant met with an accident on 19.01.2014 and filed claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest.

The Tribunal considering the NC: 2026:KHC:6408 HC-KAR entire evidence on record granted an amount of Rs.10,31,000/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from date of pitch and till date of deposit.
3. Aggrieved by the said award, the petitioner-claimant has preferred this appeal and mainly contented that it is a case of amputation of right leg below knee.
The petitioner is suffering from permanent physical disability of 80% to the right leg and 35% to the whole body, but the Tribunal granted meagre amounts under the other heads.

It is further stated that petitioner was earning Rs.15,000/- per month as he is working as a driver in Vydehi Institute of Dental Sciences and Research Centre, but the Tribunal considered his income as Rs.11,000/- per month.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 4. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for both sides.

5. Learned counsel for respondent has stated that even as per the permanent partial disability mentioned in Schedule II of Employees' Compensation Act, the amputation below knee NC:
2026:KHC:6408 HC-KAR with stump exceeding 50%, but not more than that.
Learned counsel for the appellant argued that the petitioner was working as a driver, and after the amputation, he could not discharge his duties as a driver.

Therefore, his functional disability is to be taken as 100%
instead of 35% taken by the Tribunal, whereas the learned counsel for respondent also stated that even as per Schedule I of EC Act, it was only 50%.
PW3 doctor assessed the disability as 80%.
It is stated by PW3 that the petitioner suffered 80% to the right leg and 16% to the left leg.

6. Petitioner sustained the following injuries:
Type III compound communited fracture of right leg and he has sustained compound fracture of mallelous let leg and type II acromia deprivation o left leg, and his right leg below knee was amputated.
7.
The doctor assessed the disability as 35% to the whole body.
The Tribunal also considered the same.
No doubt, petitioner cannot discharge his duties as a driver due to the injuries sustained in the accident, but, it cannot be said that he cannot do any other work.

Therefore, considering the amputation of the right leg below knee and the medical NC: 2026:KHC:6408 HC-KAR evidence and other relevant factors, this Court finds it reasonable to take the disability as 50% instead of 35%.
The petitioner filed pay slips to show that his salary was Rs.11,031/- per month, and he was aged 48 years as his date of birth is shown as 01.06.1966 and the multiplier is 13.
The petitioner is also entitled for future prospects of 25%.

Thus, the loss of future earning capacity comes to Rs.10,75,523/- (11,031+ 25% x 12 x 13 x 50%).
8.
Petitioner was inpatient for 15 days and he spent Rs.1,51,639/- towards medical expenses as per Exhibit P19.
The Tribunal granted Rs.1,52,000/- under the medical expenses and it is confirmed.

So, considering the nature of injuries, period of hospitalisation and other relevant factors, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- for pain and suffering, Rs.60,000/- for loss of amenities and Rs.60,000/- for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.
Petitioner might not have attended any other work at least for a period of 6 months.

Therefore,
Rs.66,186/- (11,031 x6) is granted towards loss of income during laid-up period.

The Tribunal granted Rs.75,000/- towards artificial limb, but this Court finds it reasonable to NC:
2026:KHC:6408 HC-KAR grant an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- for artificial limb as it is to be changed periodically.
Thus, in all, the claimant is entitled for the compensation of Rs.16,13,709/- with interest at 6% per annum as against Rs.10,31,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

9. The award of compensation passed by the Tribunal is modified as under:

 1. Loss of future income 10,75,523/-

(i) Appeal is allowed in part.
NC: 2026:KHC:6408 HC-KAR
(ii) The Claimant is entitled for the total compensation of Rs.16,13,709/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.

(iii) The respondent No.3-insurance company has already deposited the award amount before the Tribunal, and therefore, they are directed to deposit the enhanced amount of Rs.5,82,709/- with interest at 6% per annum within one month from the date of this order.
(iv) On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with the interest accrued on it.
